title: Cholesterol
caption: Four fused rings (three six-membered, one five-membered) with a hydrocarbon tail and a single –OH. The rings and tail are hydrophobic, so cholesterol sits among the phospholipid tails of an animal cell membrane, with its small polar –OH near the heads.
alt: Structure of cholesterol, C27H46O, with its four fused carbon rings shaded and its single hydroxyl group.
description: Four fused carbon rings: A, B and C are six-membered, D is five-membered.
A hydrocarbon side chain on ring D, and a small hydroxyl group on ring A.
Eight chiral centres fix its shape exactly; C₂₇H₄₆O.
